title: Women's National Coalition and the Women's Charter, South Africa
summary: South African women from political parties and civil society founded the Women's National Coalition in April 1992, after being left out of the CODESA constitutional talks. It consulted women nationwide and drafted the Women's Charter for Effective Equality to press for gender equality in the new constitution.

uncertainty.note: Founding is dated 25–26 April 1992 in one scholarly article; other sources give only April 1992.

as_recorded.value: April 1992, women from various political and civil society organizations formed the Women's National Coalition

where.historical_name: Johannesburg, Transvaal Province, Republic of South Africa

importance.justification: A cross-party coalition that won recognition of gender equality in South Africa's transition constitution.

reviewer_note: The id says 26 April; the LitNet article gives the workshop as 25–26 April, other sources only April 1992, so the day is uncertain. Member counts differ by source (40+, 54, 60, 90+) and are left out. The Charter itself (drafting, 1994 adoption) is described in the summary only in general terms; its dates were not confirmed on an opened page. Venue within Johannesburg not confirmed.
